thread:
mira: ran a fairness sweep this morning across 5 tenant classes (low/med/high + two synthetic heavy tails). attaching quick notes and numbers below.

alex: nice, did you use the replay harness or synthetic QPS?

mira: replay harness for tenants A/B/C, synthetic for D/E to stress KV-cache churn. command: `./tools/replay_harness --workload=multi_tenant_sweep --concurrency=200 --duration=15m`

sam: quick summary plz — what changed vs the last run?

mira: three config knobs we toggled: `batch_size_cap` (32/64), `max_delay_ms` (8/16/32), and kernel selection policy (legacy vs hybrid-kernel-sel). also forced KV cache cold-starts between tenants (ttl flush).

jordan: hybrid-kernel-sel == what we discussed (heuristic picks based on seq_len distribution + microbench)?

mira: yeah. heuristic picks favored fused-attn kernels for seq <= 768, else fallback. also we enabled prefetch for KV loads in GPU.

mira: results (p50/p95 p99 latencies, and cost-proxy we use tokens/sec normalized):
```
Tenant A (prod like): batch_cap=64, max_delay=16 -> p50 42ms, p95 128ms, p99 320ms, tokens/s 78
Tenant B (interactive): batch_cap=32, max_delay=8  -> p50 28ms, p95 95ms,  p99 280ms, tokens/s 62
Tenant C (burst): batch_cap=64, max_delay=32 -> p50 55ms, p95 210ms, p99 540ms, tokens/s 102
Tenant D (synthetic churn): batch_cap=32, max_delay=16 -> p50 60ms, p95 620ms, p99 1.2s, tokens/s 40
Tenant E (long-tail): batch_cap=64, max_delay=16 -> p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 1.6s, tokens/s 34
```

mira: notable: Tenant D had large p95 oscillations when KV hit-rate dipped below ~30%. We saw oscillation periods ~30-90s where queueing built up, batches hit cap and suddenly drained.

alex: that sounds like interplay between KV warmup and batching heuristics — cache miss -> slower token generation -> other tenants pack into batches -> latency spike -> fallback kernel?

mira: exactly. profiling traces show kernel selection flipping during spikes. stack excerpt from perf trace: `kv_read_wait -> scheduling_enqueue -> select_kernel(hybrid) -> fallback_to_generic` repeatedly.

sam: can you paste the short perf snippet?

mira: sure:
```
[trace snippet]
2026-03-10T09:12:15.342Z mira-node-3 GPU0: kv_lookup 1.2ms -> hit
2026-03-10T09:12:16.128Z mira-node-3 GPU0: kv_lookup 12.8ms -> miss+fetch
2026-03-10T09:12:16.136Z mira-node-3 GPU0: enqueue wait 25ms
2026-03-10T09:12:16.170Z mira-node-3 GPU0: select_kernel fused_attn
2026-03-10T09:12:16.172Z mira-node-3 GPU0: runtime fallback generic_attn (seq_len 1024)
```

jordan: fallback to generic_attn for seq_len 1024 explains the jump — kernel mismatch multiplies token latency. Any regression vs last week's hybrid-kernel-sel?

mira: yes, small regression: hybrid-kernel-sel picks slightly different kernels after prefetch change. p95 increased ~8% on average for mixed workloads. I think our cost model weighting underestimates KV latency variance.

alex: do we see batch size cap interacting with this? e.g., larger cap makes oscillation more pronounced?

mira: larger batch_cap (64) increases drain spikes when the slow tenant recovers — the fast tenants get batched more and then the kernel selector sees different seq_len distributions, making fallback frequency higher. smaller cap (32) smooths it but increases per-token cost for steady workloads.

sam: so it's a tradeoff: fairness vs unit cost. Any A/B compares with strict tenant quotas?

mira: ran a quota-enforced replay where tenant shares are pinned; oscillation amplitude decreased (~40% lower p95 spikes) but overall tokens/s dropped ~12%.

jordan: action items?

mira: proposed next steps:
- tune hybrid-kernel-sel cost model to include KV latency variance factor (alpha term)
- try asynchronous KV prefetch earlier in pipeline to reduce enqueue wait
- add adaptive batch_cap per-tenant: lower cap when tenant KV miss-rate high
- run apples-to-apples long-run (1h) with quota vs no-quota to gather economics

alex: +1 to adaptive batch_cap. Can we implement simple heuristic first? e.g., if tenant kv_miss_rate_15s > 0.3 then cap=16 else cap=64.

mira: yep I have a small patch ready. will bench it tomorrow morning. patch: `runtime/scheduler/adaptive_cap.py` ~30 LOC.

ci-bot: mira pushed branch mira/adaptive-cap-heuristic (CI: queued) :white_check_mark:

sam: please add perf harness job to run the branch against the same replay traces used here (multi_tenant_sweep).

mira: will do. scheduling it now. link to job when done: [perf job link]

alex: thanks — and capture KV hit-rate time-series in the dashboard so we can correlate spikes easily.

mira: added a dash: /dashboards/eng-runtime/fairness-sweep-1834567890 with p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, batch_sizes, kernel_choice over time.

jordan: nice. If adaptive cap helps reduce p95 spikes without killing tokens/s then we can stage it as an opt-in rollout behind a flag.

mira: agreed. I'll post results in #eng-runtime once the longer run completes.

alex: :thumbsup:
